author: TEDx Talks
description:
Everyone makes mistakes—but the heartbeat of who we are is revealed in the seconds after. This talk invites us to trade defensiveness for courage: name the misstep, own the impact, and take action to repair. Accountability isn’t a public confession; it’s a practical promise that restores dignity and rebuilds trust. When leaders model honest responsibility, individuals and teams feel safe to speak up, learn faster, and grow stronger together. Repair over perfection creates cultures where people can be imperfect and still be dependable. Choose repair—and you don’t just recover from failure; you reshape what’s possible. 

Pearl Moses is Compliance Director at Setfords Law Ltd and a solicitor with several years’ experience in regulatory compliance, legal publishing, and private practice. Formerly Risk and Compliance Lead at the Law Society of England and Wales, she has held senior regulatory roles and serves on the Law Society’s Legal Compliance Bulletin’s editorial board. Pearl is a soug
title: How to repair a relationship in 3 steps | Pearl Moses | TEDxArden University Manchester

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Build the data center—or block it? That yes-or-no debate can leave important questions unanswered. Undergraduate student Ian Sun explores what becomes possible when communities can see more of the tradeoffs and ask where, how and with whose input these facilities should be built. Ian Sun believes innovation must work for the people who have to live with its consequences. 

An electrical engineering and computer science student at MIT, he builds technology to tackle real-world problems. 

A sustainability hackathon led him to explore AI’s physical footprint and how better data can give communities a voice in shaping the infrastructure behind it. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Data Centers: What Lies Beyond Yes or No? | Ian Sun | TEDxAtlanta Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At eight, Temple Lester went to science camp to build rockets. Instead, she was asked to help the boys. Years later, she began questioning something adults say to children with the best intentions: “You are the future.” Could those encouraging words be keeping young people on the sidelines? STEM advocate Temple Lester has spent nearly a decade helping young people recognize the power of their ideas and imagination.

A physics student and Karsh STEM Scholar at Howard University, Temple founded STEM Girl Swag and has been recognized as a Coca-Cola Scholar, Time Kid of the Year finalist and White House honoree. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Problem With Calling Young People “The Future” | Temple Lester | TEDxAtlanta Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ever had an idea you talked yourself out of before anyone else could reject it? After decades in the entertainment and media industry, Genevieve LeDoux knew that feeling well. Then a question from a five-year-old challenged everything she thought she knew about experience, creativity, and whose ideas deserve to be heard. Genevieve LeDoux has spent her career turning imagination into stories and questioning what happens to creativity when we get too good at knowing the rules.

An Emmy-winning producer, songwriter and storyteller, Genevieve has spent nearly two decades creating entertainment for young audiences. Her work spans television, music, animation and interactive media, bringing together artists, writers and technologists to build worlds designed to capture a child’s imagination.

Today, Genevieve is the creator of Star Forest, an animated musical universe inspired by nature, music and the wonderfully unconventional ways children see the world. Through her work, she continues to
title: How one unexpected voice can change everything | Genevieve LeDoux | TEDxAtlanta

author: TEDx Talks
description: Cities around the world are investing billions of dollars to attract tourists by building stadiums, resorts, convention centers, and entertainment districts, including many projects emerging across the Washington, D.C. region. Yet, places that pursue the same strategy often see very different results. Some destinations experience strong economic growth, new jobs, and vibrant local businesses, while others struggle with overcrowded infrastructure, rising housing costs, and pressure on natural and cultural resources. How can the same strategy lead to such different outcomes? Kimberly’s research explores why tourism benefits some destinations while straining others. In her talk, she reveals the key questions to ask about new development to ensure we strengthen destinations rather than strain them. Dr. Kimberly Clarke is a public policy professional, researcher, and speaker based in the Washington, D.C. area. She holds a PhD from Southern New Hampshire University, holds degrees from Johns
title: Ask these three questions about new tourist developments | Kimberly Clarke | TEDxLogan Circle

author: TEDx Talks
description: Un ponte si interrompe a mezz’aria, eppure nell’acqua il suo riflesso appare intero. In quel dipinto Stefano Zaccaria riconosce qualcosa che accade quando proviamo a dare forma a un’idea: riusciamo a intravedere ciò che potrebbe diventare mentre stiamo ancora cercando il modo di costruirla. Il coraggio entra in gioco quando decidiamo che vale la pena cominciare e raccontiamo quell’idea a qualcuno. A volte, proprio raccontandola, scopriamo che altri vedono una possibilità dove noi vedevamo soltanto un desiderio. Da quel momento, scegliere una direzione può diventare una responsabilità condivisa. Stefano Zaccaria è direttore marketing di Toyota Material Handling Italia dal 2021, nel settore dell’intralogistica e della movimentazione delle merci. Ha iniziato la carriera nella produzione presso Pineider, dove ha poi assunto la direzione commerciale e marketing. È stato amministratore delegato di Antiche Officine Pineider e vicepresidente per le vendite globali e il marketing di K-array, a
title: Il coraggio di avere Coraggio | Stefano Zaccaria | TEDxSiena

author: TEDx Talks
description: Mandeep’s TED Talk explores how discipline, education, and perseverance shaped his journey from a shy student to a practising advocate. Through his personal experiences and career challenges, he highlights the importance of personal growth and self-belief. Recognising the complexity of Indian law for ordinary citizens, he began simplifying legal concepts through Instagram, making legal awareness more accessible. His journey emphasises that education goes beyond degreeS, it is about growth, purpose, and creating meaningful impact. Mandeep Baisala is an Advocate at the Supreme Court of India, with experience in litigation and legal practice. Beyond the courtroom, he is involved in legal education and mentorship, helping aspiring lawyers navigate the profession with clarity and confidence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: Annamaria Torre aveva quindici anni quando vide suo padre, Marcello Torre, assassinato dalla camorra. Era sindaco di Pagani, la sua città d’origine. Nella lettera che lasciò alla famiglia scrisse di sognare una Pagani civile e libera. Il suo impegno per la città passava anche dal dire «no» alle infiltrazioni della camorra negli appalti pubblici. Oggi Annamaria porta quella storia nelle scuole e chiede ai ragazzi quanto pesa dire «no» di fronte a un illecito o a un’ingiustizia, quando voltarsi dall’altra parte sarebbe più facile. Nel suo racconto, fare memoria significa trasmettere il coraggio di prendere posizione anche quando si ha paura. Annamaria Torre è impegnata nella testimonianza civile e nell’educazione alla legalità. Aveva quindici anni quando suo padre Marcello, avvocato e sindaco di Pagani, fu assassinato dalla camorra l’11 dicembre 1980. Oggi presiede l’Associazione Marcello Torre, nata per iniziativa della madre Lucia De Palma, che organizza il Premio Nazionale per l’Impe
title: La memoria non resta in silenzio | Annamaria Torre | TEDxSiena

author: TEDx Talks
description:
I was twelve, watching television, when a dancer introduced himself as a graphic designer. I had no idea what the words meant. Then he performed, the screen behind him moved with him, and I understood one thing without understanding any of it. He wasn't designing graphics; he was speaking with it.

He didn't know he was giving me something. Nor did the strangers who gave me free tutorials. Much of what I know, I owe to people who will never know my name.

Graphic design was never a profession. It was a language only a few people were allowed to speak. That permission is gone, because another stranger is giving it away without knowing. AI will hand anyone a fluent-looking image in three seconds. No tutorials, no six years. Everyone receives it, asked or not. That's how languages spread.

Once AI makes everyone fluent, fluency stops being worth much. What's left is who can read it. Every ad, every thumbnail you scroll past decides how you feel before you've read a word, and most of us c
title: The Language You Already Speak | Gan-Erdene Boldbaatar | TEDxShildeg School Youth

In his TEDx talk, “Maya of Success,” the speaker shares his journey in the acting industry and reflects on the factors that have shaped his success. He talks about his passion for acting, how he entered the industry, and the joy he found in pursuing something he truly loved. His journey highlights the importance of following one’s passion and staying committed to it despite the challenges that may arise along the way.
The speaker believes that two important elements contribute to success: hard work and spirituality. According to him, success is not achieved overnight but is the result of consistent effort, dedication, and belief in oneself. He emphasises that the achievements he has earned throughout his journey are a reflection of the hard work he has put in and the consistency with which he has pursued his goals. Through his experiences, he encourages people to remain focused on their ambitions, trust the process, and understand that true success comes from a combination of persiste
title: Maya of success  | Keshav Sadhna | TEDxMAIMS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What do you see when you look in the mirror? And more importantly, how much of what you see is shaped by your own beliefs and the judgments of others?

In this talk, Dr. Anmol Chugh explores how appearance-based judgments can influence the way we see ourselves. Through examples from his work as a plastic surgeon, he highlights the difference between changing how we look and changing how we feel about ourselves. A physical transformation may improve a feature, but it cannot automatically create confidence, happiness or a sense of self-worth.

He introduces the idea of refining your reflection and shares a simple framework built around the five vowels: Accept, Explore, Impact, Own and Uplift. His message is that self-worth is not something we need to earn. It begins with accepting who we are, discovering our potential and being kind to ourselves and others. Dr. Anmol Chugh is a board-certified plastic and cosmetic surgeon with expertise in facial and breast surgeries. As a specialist in
title: The Mirror Never Called You Ugly? | Dr Anmol Chugh | TEDxAravali Intl School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if a small conversation today could change someone's life 20 years from now? What if a few words of encouragement could become the reason someone finds the confidence to pursue a completely different path?

In this talk, Vijay Sampathkumar explores the lasting impact of everyday interactions. Drawing from his own career journey, a meaningful professional connection and the inspiring story of his wife, he reflects on how seemingly ordinary moments can create extraordinary outcomes over time.

He also challenges us to rethink how we guide the next generation. Instead of preparing children for a future we cannot predict, we should help them become ready for uncertainty through encouragement, curiosity and positive reinforcement.

His message is simple: the words we speak and the belief we show in others today may become the echoes that guide their tomorrow. Vijay Sampathkumar is a technology and business leader with over three decades of experience in IT infrastructure, global busin
title: Echoes of Tomorrow: The Impact We Leave Behind | Vijay Sampathkumar | TEDxAravali Intl School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
You have the degree, the skills and the qualifications. So why aren't employers noticing you?

In this talk, Shubham Gupta explores the gap between being qualified for a job and being chosen for one. Through a real-life recruitment story, he explains how a candidate went from receiving no interview calls to securing four interviews and a job offer in just 12 days, without gaining any new skills. The difference was how his experience was presented.

Shubham identifies three reasons talented candidates often go unnoticed: they learn to collect qualifications rather than demonstrate results, write applications for themselves rather than the person reading them, and hesitate to communicate their achievements. He shares a practical three-step approach: understand the employer's problem, prove you can solve it, and explain your value in the employer's language.

His message is clear: talent matters, but people need to see the evidence behind it. Shubham Gupta is a recruitment leader and car
title: The Translation Gap: Why Talent Goes Unnoticed | Shubham Gupta | TEDxAravali Intl School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What makes something strong enough to carry weight? In a steel foundry, strength is not decided when molten metal is poured into a mould. It is determined much earlier, through the quality of the material, the preparation and the decisions made along the way.

Drawing from his journey as a fourth-generation steel industry entrepreneur, Naman Sood connects the principles of manufacturing with the way we build our character. He shares three lessons: keep your promises because trust is earned through consistency, pay attention to what and who influences you because your inputs shape your future, and take responsibility beyond what is expected because finishing the work makes you dependable.

He also reflects on a major business setback early in his career and how it became a turning point for learning and growth.

His message to young people is simple: you don't become strong and then carry the weight. You carry the weight, and then you become strong. Naman Sood is an entrepreneur and fo
title: Built to Carry: The Weight of Your Word | Naman Sood | TEDxAravali Intl School Youth

description: Kasdienybėje dažnai stengiamės atsiriboti nuo temų, kurios kelia nerimą ir nepatogumą. Vengimas kalbėti apie mirtį – vienas iš to pavyzdžių. Kaip tyrėja ir lektorė bendradarbiauja su įvairiomis institucijomis, aktyviai dalyvauja mokslo komunikacijos bei populiarinimo veiklose. description: Eva-Rose's talk challenges the common view that psychology is only about mental illness, showing instead how positive psychology uses research to focus on purpose, resilience, and well-being, and how these ideas can be applied to improve everyday life, especially for students. Eva-Rose is a passionate student who is a trilingual speaker in French, Spanish, and English who embraces creativity through painting and art, while also pursuing her passion for writing, with several of her works published. In her free time, she studies and researches psychology, deepening her understanding of human behavior and well-being. On campus, she tutors students in AP European History, all levels of French, and Chemistry Honors. She is also actively involved in the theater company Broken Box, where she continues to explore performance and storytelling. author: TEDx Talks
description: Entre el golpe y la respuesta explora una pregunta profundamente humana: ¿Dónde vive nuestra libertad cuando ya no podemos controlar lo que ocurre? A partir de una experiencia personal que puso en crisis mis certezas, la charla propone recorrer ese momento en el que la vida deja de responder a nuestros planes y nos obliga a mirar hacia un lugar diferente: nuestra capacidad de elegir quién queremos ser frente a aquello que no podemos cambiar. De este recorrido surge el concepto de Soberanía Personal: ese territorio interior que existe entre lo que nos sucede y la respuesta que elegimos dar. Senior HR Mentor en Marca Personal y Liderazgo. This includes basketball, track and field, and a little bit of cooking. He is not passionate about many things, but when he is, he is always determined to do his best until he can no longer continue. A student who is seen by many through a thousand different lenses but believes in his true self and who he really is. author: TEDx Talks
description: A ativista Júlia Bonitese Duarte aborda em sua palestra a emergência climática sob a perspectiva do adultocentrismo e do racismo ambiental, defendendo que as crianças não devem ser excluídas das decisões ecológicas do presente. No contexto contemporâneo, marcado pelo agravamento das crises socioambientais e pela desigualdade nos impactos do aquecimento global, a mensagem destaca a força do ativismo cotidiano e familiar iniciado pelos mais jovens. Dessa forma, o tema redefine o conceito de legado: em vez de consistir em uma herança pronta deixada pelos adultos para o futuro, o verdadeiro legado é cocriado com as novas gerações, empoderando suas vozes e valorizando pequenas ações diárias que geram transformação coletiva duradoura.  Júlia Bonitese é ativista ambiental desde os 8 anos, fundou o Projeto Pequenos Protetores do Planeta, é membro de organizações nacionais e internacionais e atuou na COP30. title: Ativismo de Sofá: Como Pequenas Ações Podem Salvar o Planeta | Júlia Bonitese | TEDxSete Lagoas
